key_insight: A Pareto-front multi-objective optimization constructs content-adaptive, quality-monotonic bitrate ladders for VVC streaming that jointly trade off bitrate, visual quality, and decoding complexity. This yields more efficient adaptive streaming decisions than single-objective heuristics.
problem_solved: Adaptive streaming must balance bitrate, perceived quality, and decoder complexity per content and codec; existing ladders are often static or optimize only one metric, causing suboptimal network or device-level performance.
method: Formulate bitrate, video quality (e.g., objective quality metric), and decoding complexity as simultaneous optimization objectives and compute the Pareto front of coding configurations.
Select quality-monotonic, content-adaptive bitrate ladder points from the Pareto front to ensure increasing quality with bitrate while meeting complexity constraints.
Integrate the resulting ladders into VVC streaming workflows so the client/server can make informed adaptation choices under varying bandwidth and device capabilities.
impact: Enables streaming systems and ML-driven adaptation agents to make principled trade-offs across bitrate, quality, and compute cost—improving user experience and resource efficiency for diverse content and devices.

paper_title: Multi-Objective Pareto-Front Optimization for Efficient Adaptive VVC Streaming
paper_authors: Angeliki Katsenou, Vignesh V. Menon, Guoda Laurinaviciute, Benjamin Bross, Detlev Marpe
